1. Development Description of ESP32

1.1 Introduction of on-board ESP32 configuration

SEA on-board ESP32 use ESP32-D0WDQ6 solution in ESP32 Series of ESPRESSIF, ESP32 chip is shown in the
figure below (should be ESP32-D0WDQ6- 2J2018-TUBOPHPU07)

The specific configuration is as follows:
• Equipped with WIFI solution (2.4GHz), and use 802.11 b/g/n standard

• Equipped with Bluetooth solution (v4.2 standard), compatible with traditional Bluetooth (BR/EDR) and low
power consumption Bluetooth (BLE)
• CPU uses a 32-bit Lx6 single/dual core processor, with a computing power of up to 600MIPS, and internal
ROM (448KB), SRAM (520KB), RTC SRAM (16KB)
• Equipped with off-chip SPI interface FLASH (W25Q32JVZPIG), 32-bit, 4M storage, 1024 sectors, 64 blocks,
each block is 64K bytes, and supports clock speeds up to 80MHz

2. Front Installation Description of ESP32
2.1 Driver installation

The on-board ESP32 needs to be connected to the PC through a Type-C cable, and the driver is CP210x USB (for
different computer needs, you can visit Silicon Labs Official Website for download), the specific installation steps are
as follows:

(1) Connect one end of the Type-C cable to the computer and the other end to the SEA board, and power on

(2) Open the PC device manager and check the port information. If there is no CP210x in the port, then there will be
a triangle exclamation mark in the universal serial bus controller to indicate that there is no driver.
(3) Visit the official website to download the corresponding USB driver (or use it directly in the attachment package)

(4) After decompressing the compressed package, select and install according to the PC system (x64 or x86) (when
installing, the board needs to be powered off)

(5) After the installation is complete, power on the board again, and the following information can be seen in the
device manager, which means the installation is complete

(6) If the installation fails, check whether the driver is selected correctly (ESP32 and Type-C have been tested
before the board leaves the factory)
2.2 Firmware programming

For SEA on-board ESP32, the firmware has been burnt before leaving the factory by default. However, for different
usage scenarios, users can customize the firmware for programming. The programming tools can be downloaded
from ESPRESSIF official website (or directly use Flash Download Tools in the attachment package), where the
download on the official website is as follows:

The programming steps are as follows:
(1)Run the exe file named flash_download_tool_3.8.5 in the folder (Note: The downloaded version may not be exactly
the same)

(2) Select Developer Mode

(3) Select ESP32 Download Tool

(4) Wait for 3-4 seconds,and then enter the following interface

(5) Select the firmware (bin file) that needs to be programmed. The default is the bin file provided by SEA official
(different from the initial ESP32 firmware), and select the correct port (check in the device manager, it may not be
consistent with the port in the screenshot), other default configuration, baud rate up to 921600.

(6) Press and hold the BOOT button on the board

(7) Click START, when the progress bar starts to read, you can release the BOOT button (Note: If there is an ERROR
situation after releasing it, it means that you must press and hold BOOT during firmware programming)

(8) After the programming is completed, the effect is as follows

3. Description of ESP32 Development Platform

ESP32 programming development is divided into Micro-Python platform and Arduino IDE platform according to the
different needs of users. The reference opinions are as follows:

•
Developers are accustomed to using python language or have been experienced in micro-python
language, and the Micro-Python platform is recommended.
•
Development projects need to simplify the code structure and require low difficulty in entry-level, and
the Micro-Python platform is recommended
•
Developers are accustomed to using C language or proficient in Arduino IDE, Arduino IDE platform is
recommended
•
For development projects that require better interaction and require high algorithm complexity, the
Arduino IDE platform is recommended

(Note: For more technical reference materials of ESP32, you can find on ESPRESSIF Official Website)

3.1 Configuration of Micro-Python development environment

There are many options for Micro-Python development tools. At present, the offline execution tool uPyCraft that does
not need to be installed is more suitable (provided in the attachment package), and the standard development tools
such as ESPRESSIF IDF and thonny tools on GitHub are available.

Considering the installation and use experience, this document introduces the uPyCraft and the thonny tools.

Before the introduction, you need to prepare a TF card, connect it to the PC through a card reader, convert it to FAT32
format through formatting operations (do not format quickly), and then create an Overlay folder in the root directory of
the TF card and store it inside bit file and create a board_config.json file in the root directory. The content of the file is
as follows:



"Board_Info": {
"board_name": "SEA",
"version:": [
0, 1, 0
],
"relese_date":[
2019,6,2


"Board_Setup": {
"WIFI_config": {
"enable": "false",
"ssid": "None",
"password": "None"
3.1.1 Software use of uPyCraft
For uPyCraft software, briefly introduce the following interface components. In addition to the conventional selections
in the top toolbar, on the right side of the interface, from top to bottom, create a new file, open a file, save this file,
download and run, stop , connect to the serial port, backward, forward, grammar check, clear the console output.

The specific use process is as follows:

(1) Open the py file that needs to be downloaded to ESP32 (it can be opened via Open on the right or File->Open on
the top toolbar)

"FTP_config":{
"enable":"false"

"boot_on_SDcard":"false"

"Overlay_List": [
"system_wrapper.bit",
"Camera_Demo.bit"

(2) Connect the SEA board to the PC via Type-C and power on, click Tools->Serial in the toolbar at the top of the
software to select the serial port (or Connect paperclip symbol in the shortcut bar directly on the right), you need to
pay attention to the following two points

•
If the words "open serial error, please try again" appear, you need to connect the serial port again (it belongs to software
bug, it can be normal after 2-3 times)

•
If “ > > program is running, do anything with stop it! 1” appears, you need to wait for 3-4 seconds, wait for “program is
running, do anything with stop it! 2” to appear on the console, and then connect the serial port again (reason: the original
program in esp32 is running)

Note: If the firmware is not programmed or programmed incorrectly, the serial port must not be connected
The connection is successful as shown in the figure below:

(3) Click Tools->DownloadAndRun in the toolbar or click on the triangle on the right (Tools->Download is also
possible, you need to power on and restart to run the downloaded program)
After the download is complete, you need to pay attention to the following three points:

• If the following words appear, you need to re-power on to run the program correctly

• If the following words appear, it means normal operation

• If there are other wrong words, with SD_ If MMC reports an error, there may be four reasons: the TF
card slot is loose, the TF card file format is incorrect (FAT32 is required), the TF card file is incorrect,
and the bit file does not exist in the TF card

3.1.2 Software use of thonny

For thorny software, you can download it from its official website (or find it in the attachment package), and
the relevant project description can be found on the official GitHub. This document briefly introduces the
interface composition of thorny software. Like most ides, it is composed of toolbar, code box, console and
composition of right operation inspection mark.

After the installation is completed, set the interface language to Chinese when opening, and then click Tools >
settings to enter the following interface and select MicroPython(ESP32) in the interpreter.

The specific debugging and downloading process are as follows:

(1) Select the port of your device in the port column of settings, click OK, and it will be automatically verified

(2) Click Open (in the folder in the toolbar) to view the device file, and select the MicroPython device

(3) Enter the Flash, check the programmed py file, delete and open the file (click the file, right-click to select)

(4) You can click the py file to modify the content, or you can add other files, such as creating a new file, click
Save, and select the MicroPython device (or directly open the original file, click File -> Save as, select the
MicroPython device)

(5) Then enter the saved file name and click OK

(6) After saving, check the file in FLASH again

3.2 Configuration of Arduino IDE development environment

For developers familiar with Arduino development, the configuration process of this development environment is
very simple, and the specific steps are as follows:

(1)Visit at Arduino Official Website to download the installation package of the Arduino corresponding to the
operating system (or directly find it in the attachment package)

(2) Click File->Preference, and add the address of Arduino core for esp32 in Additional Boards Manager URLs, and
the specific address is as follows:

https://dl.espressif.com/dl/package_esp32_index.json

(3) After adding, search and download the data package of ESP32 development board in Tools->Board->Boards
Manager

(4) Considering the slow downloading process, an offline installation method is also provided. In File->Preference,
check the location of SketchBook Location

Under the location path, enter the "./handware/espressif" folder (if the path does not exist, you need to create it
manually), and then run esp32_package_v1_0_2.exe in the attachment package, unzip the esp32 file compression
package to this directory, after unzipping, enter the esp32/tools directory, as shown in the figure:

Then, Windows users run the get.exe file, Mac users and Linux users run get.py, and automatically exit after running,
and the installation is complete.

(5) Restart Arduino IDE, you can find ESP32 Dev Module in Tools->Board, and select it.

(6) Unzip the spartan-edge-esp32-boot compressed package in the attachment package to the library folder at the
SketchBook Location in File->Preference. After unzipping, it is shown in the following figure:

(7) After the spartan-edge-esp32-boot library is installed, you can find two routines in File-> Examples -> spartan-
edge-esp32-boot (at the bottom) of the Arduino IDE.

(8) Open the routine "02LoadConfigBitstream", load it into ESP32 after compiling, and then load the bitstream in the
TF card into FPGA on the ESP32 side. After the configuration is complete, verification is required.The verification
steps are as follows:

(1) Prepare a TF card (now commonly called SD card with small size), connect it to the PC through a card reader, and format it in
FAT32 format (don't select quick format), and create the file "board_ config.ini " under the root directory of TF card, write the following
;board infomation

[Board_Info]
board_name = SEA
version = 0,1,0
relese_date = 2019,7,22



;WIFI setting about board
[WIFI_config]
enable = false
ssid = None
password = None


;FTP setting about board
[FTP_config]
enable = false



;setup status about board
[Board_Setup]
boot_on_SDcard = false
overlay_on_boot = system_wrapper.bit
overlay_actions_comment = always, onbutton, none
overlay_actions = always




;the overlay list
[Overlay_List_Info]
Overlay_List = system_wrapper.bit Camera_Demo.bit
Overlay_Dir = /overlay/
(2) Where, "overlay_on_boot" is the bitstream file automatically loaded after power-on, and "Overlay_List" is the bitstream file in all
overlay folders.

(3) Insert the TF card into the TF card slot of the SEA board, and set the DIP switch "Slave-JTAG" to Slave mode.

(4) Connect the SEA board to the PC via the Type-C cable and power it on, select the development board as "ESP32 Dev Module" in
the Arduino IDE, and select the corresponding port in the tool

(5) Click "Upload" to program and download ESP32. After Connecting appears, if the automatic connection is not made, press the boot
button on the development board and release it, repeat the above steps until the connection is completed, the subsequent download will
be automatically performed; the debugging interface is displayed as follows:

(6) After the ESP32 program is downloaded, open the serial monitor of the Arduino IDE, set the baud rate to 115200, press the RST
button of the development board to reset the ESP32, if the serial monitor displays as follows:

It means that the bitstream of FPGA is successfully loaded, and the "FPGA_DONE" indicator on the development board will light up.

After the ESP32 program is successfully loaded, you can add the bitstream file to be changed or added to the "overlay" directory of
the TF card, or change the "board_config.ini" file in the TF card to modify the FPGA automatic loading.
(7) The following error occurred：

1. The serial monitor will display:

E (78) sdmmc_sd: sdmmc_init_sd_scr: send_scr (1) returned
0x109 Card Mount Failed,please reboot the board
The solution is as follows:
• TF card slot is loose
• The bit file is missing from the TF card file
• TF card is damaged
• After the bit file in the Overlay folder is modified, the "board_config.ini" file in the TF card is not changed to modify the
FPGA automatic loading.

2. The serial monitor reported the following error:

The solution is as follows:
• The TF card file is not placed in the correct format, just put the board_config.ini file in the root directory.

3. Run the program that loads the bit file in the Arduino IDE and report an error: cannot find the implementation of
the function sdmmc_host_pullup_en

The solution is as follows:
ESP32 firmware programming error, need to re-program the firmware
•
The ESP32 library installed by Arduino IDE is incomplete, so it is required to install such library for SD_MMC

4. When using Arduino IDE to load the Bit file, the serial monitor reports an error:

The solution is as follows:
• Without clicking the “Upload” button in Arduino IDE, only click the verification, which means that the local program is
compiled, and only by clicking upload will the program be downloaded to ESP32

5. When using Arduino IDE to load the Bit file, the serial monitor displays the following message:

The solution is as follows:
• The TF card pins are in poor contact, or the TF card slot is loose, you need to press the TF card slot pins and wipe
the TF card pins
The bit file in the TF card is damaged or wrong

6. When loading the bit file to FPGA by TF card, if the bit file was originally in the form of "Chinese.bit" and changed to the
form of "English.bit", the loading is unsuccessful, and the error displayed is as follows:

The solution is as follows:
• The computer defaults to Chinese. The bit is utf-8 encoding, and you need to change the English twice to return to
normal
• Opened with notepad/sublime/notepad/writing board,the default encoding is utf-8, if you save it when closed, it will
become utf-8 encoding

7. When using ESP32 to load bit files to FPGA, the serial monitor shows the following error "Failed to mount filesystem on
SDcard":

The solution is as follows:
• TF card is damaged
• The file system format of the TF card is not FAT32, so it cannot be recognized. It needs to be formatted as a FAT32 file
system, and do not check the quick format

8. When using ESP32 to load a bit file to FPGA, the following garbled message appears on the serial monitor:

The solution is as follows:
• The board_config.ini file in the TF card was opened with notepad, and input and saved in Chinese format, causing part

4.1 Micro-Python development

When ESP32 programming development is based on the Micro-Python development platform, the Micro-Python
firmware run by ESP32 is built on MicroPython_LoBo and add a module library for loading Bit files to FPGA-xfpga

For information about MicroPython_LoBo and use cases of Micro-Python modules, you can refer to
MicroPython_LoBo wiki.


4.1.1 Introduction of Micro-Python library

The MicroPython library is divided into three parts.

• The first part is built by combining the basic library of Python and the hardware characteristics of ESP32. At the same time,
the naming is slightly different for distinguishing. For example, the json module in Python is renamed ujson in MicroPython, but
you can use both json and ujson names.

• The second part is unique to embedded, such as the machine library that contains on-chip resource operations such as CPU
and peripherals, and the network library that contains network processing

• The third part is unique to specific modules. For example, there is an esp32 library for esp32
For specific library introduction, please refer to MicroPython Official Document。

4.1.2 Usage examples of GPIO in Micro-Python development

The ESP32 chip has 40 GPIO pads. However, some GPIO pads cannot be used or there are no corresponding pins
on the chip package (see ESP32 Technical Reference Manual)

The following two points need to be paid attention:
• The available IOs are 0-19, 21-23, 25-27, 32-39
• GPIO1 and GPIO3 are TX and RX of UART0 respectively, which are the ports for programming and default debugging
• GPIO6-11 is usually used for SPI Flash
• GPIO34-39 can only be set to input mode, there is no software pull-up or pull-down function

4.2 Arduino IDE development

Regarding the development of ESP32 on the Arduino IDE, most of the basic cases are included in the ESP32 library.
You can open File->Examples->ESP32 in the Arduino IDE to view the basic cases. Some basic operations such as
GPIO, Serial, etc.are the same as on Arduino.

For Arduino IDE to perform WIFI, IIC, SPI, IIS, IOT operations, basically you only need to call the corresponding
